title: Tailored quant profile validation playbook for customer FP8/INT8 exception
creator: Maya Patel
description: Support request from FinSecure (NDA) to run a bespoke calibration and validation for an FP8 -> INT8 fallback profile on their trading model. The customer reports intermittent accuracy regressions when using the standard FP8 profile under peak sequence lengths and would like a short-term exception with a custom quant profile plus a validated rollback strategy. This ticket defines the playbook, run steps, acceptance gates, and rollback plan for on-demand bespoke calibration runs requested by high-risk customers.
acceptance_criteria: Provide reproducible calibration artifacts (scale/zero points) for the customer model that show <=0.5% relative accuracy regression vs FP32 on the customer eval set when using FP8, or documented fallback to INT8 with <=0.2% regression.
Generate a calibration report (CSV + HTML) with per-layer quantization stats, outlier counts, and token-level delta distributions shared with the customer under NDA.
Create a validated rollback plan (model pin + routing policy) tested in staging that the customer can switch to with <5s config change and no downtime.
Documented SR-runbook and oncall escalation steps including estimated cost delta and latency impact numbers for bespoke profile usage.
Run artifacts uploaded to S3 and referenceable from the ticket; customer sign-off recorded.
Automated regression checks executed (unit prompts and production prompt sample set) with pass/fail outputs.
Security review for artifacts containing customer data completed if any sample logs are retained.
All changes limited to profile artifacts and runtime config; no model weight changes allowed for exceptions.
runbook_steps: 1) Intake: Confirm NDA, customer eval dataset location and size (min 1k samples recommended).
2) Baseline: Run deterministic FP32 vs current FP8 profile evaluation to capture baseline accuracy/loss distributions. Store outputs in s3://redwood-support/finsecure/ENG-21688/baseline/.

3) Calibration: Run bespoke calibration pipeline (per-layer histogram + MSE outlier clipping) with three candidate parameter sets (conservative, balanced, aggressive) and produce scale/zero tables for each.
4) Validation: Evaluate each candidate on customer eval set and representative production prompt sample. Collect latency and memory metrics under target batch sizes.
5) Selection: Choose the candidate that meets accuracy and latency SLOs. If none meet accuracy gates, prepare INT8 fallback candidate set and repeat validation.
6) Staging rollout: Apply profile to staging dedicated worker pool, run 24h soak with synthetic traffic and the customer's sample set. Monitor token-level deltas and error rates.
7) Sign-off: Share report with customer and request explicit written approval for production application or fallback usage.
8) Production: Apply profile to customer-dedicated route with canary at 1% traffic; monitor for 2h then ramp to requested percentage. Provide rollback toggle.
calibration_results_summary: Conservative candidate: average per-token L2 delta 0.21, top-1 label drift 0.35%, latency +2.1%
Balanced candidate: average per-token L2 delta 0.14, top-1 label drift 0.48%, latency +1.8%
Aggressive candidate: average per-token L2 delta 0.35 (failed accuracy gate), top-1 drift 1.6%, latency +1.2%
INT8 fallback candidate: per-token L2 delta 0.08, top-1 label drift 0.18%, latency +4.5% (higher memory pressure)

Rollback trigger conditions: >0.7% regression on rolling 1k prompt window OR user-reported critical correctness issues.
